body:
CORRECTION: the immediately preceding FYI was empty because noninteractive stdin closed. Actual provisional read-only P1R findings follow; this is not a candidate verdict and no repository paths were touched.

Positive evidence: runtime-handoff.json rehashes to 6dd741f6..., requirements.freeze.txt to 8557f7a3...; the live venv exactly matches all 61 frozen packages; Python, checkpoint archive/files, tokenizer files, qualification script, both output files, receipt fields, and ordered 50-outcome equality all reverified.

Repair before freezing a repository manifest:
1. Component licence: runtime-handoff.json lines 28-35 adds Unidecode 1.4.0 because amrlib omitted it, but records no licence. Installed wheel metadata says GPL and classifier GPLv2+; installed licence SHA-256 is 8177f97513213526df2cf6184d8ff986c675afb514d4e68a404010521b880643. This is not a claim that GPL forbids local use; it is a missing component/licence record.
2. Fixture identity: qualify_runtime.py lines 20-23 read a mutable repository path; lines 123-139 reimplement sentence splitting and check only count equals 50. The handoff has neither source checksum nor SurfaceAtlas/ordered canonical-unit identity. A different 50-sentence input can still yield a 50/50 receipt. Bind the admitted StorySource checksum and ordered sentence-digest vector derived from the checked repository SurfaceAtlas, plus analyzer/code identity, and refuse foreign source or segmentation.
3. Self-contained join: runtime-handoff.json line 76 names requirements.freeze.txt without its SHA; that SHA exists only in a separate message. Original amrlib and Unidecode wheel bytes are not in the handoff directory, so wheel hashes cannot be reverified from this object alone. Embed the freeze digest and resolvable external asset identities/locations; name first and second receipt files rather than relying on order.

Held-out, chart conversion, and transcript remain explicitly out of scope of this qualification and are not being misreported here.
